direct.need: a Supervisor namespace, vended to you
direct.note: usable means it publishes its own namespaceEndpointURL; that URL is the door

direct.need: a VM image THAT namespace can name
direct.note: bound to the namespace, or cluster-scoped from a library attached to the Supervisor; the Kubernetes node images in the cluster list do not count

direct.need: storage quota with room for the boot disk
direct.note: the refusal arrives from an admission webhook at the create call and names the reason

automation.need: everything the direct door needs, unchanged
automation.note: the blueprint applies the same object into the same namespace; nothing above goes away

automation.need: a project you are a member of
automation.note: the deployment is scoped to it and the catalog item is published to it
authoring changes nothing; it is a document until a version is released
the version object's name is derived, not chosen: it must equal '<blueprint>:<version>'

automation.need: a catalog item, for the catalog door only
automation.note: released with publishToCatalog true; the API door does not need this one

credentials.credentialHeld: a tenant bearer, from a session login

doors.takesInstead: a session id from POST /api/session, or Basic, as a vCenter single sign-on principal

credentials.note: a door answering 200 here is answering this identity; what it then PERMITS is the project role tier and the four dials, which the access-control chapter covers
